utterances.text: Yeah, H is Ambassador Holbrooke and the R is Larry Rossin from the State Department. I probably didn't record all of the names that were involved in the call.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What I'm interested in is this last statement here by Mr. P, in other words, Pickering: "Push hard to get them back in compliance ..." How did you understand this?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I need to read the context that that was made in because all I have is just a snap-shot. I don't know what this is in relation to myself without referring to my notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, you can read it. This is an entry for the 9th -- for the 10th, so read the whole page.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd like to go back to the pages prior to that. If you want me to comment on this, I'd like to see the prior two pages to see if I can put this in context.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: The question -- this was on the day -- one day after Racak. We can see the English page that precedes. Does this help to refresh your memory?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm waiting for the prior page, though, to come up as I asked for. If you want me to comment on this, I'd like to have the opportunity to try and refresh my own memory by looking at what was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't know if I can assist. I have a hard copy of what's the prior page from our excerpts dated the 16th of January of conversation with General Clark. I could hand that to the witness or we could go back in e-court.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Actually I just got it here, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Which is page 33 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. If I can go to the original page, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 34, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And your question of me was reference to: "Push hard to get them back in compliance - we must initiate ACTORD." And you want me to tell you what I think that means?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That as I understand it is what's asked of you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When Racak went down this was obviously a major event and a major turning point for the KVM mission because it was up until this point probably the worst event that we had faced as a mission. Ambassador Walker was informing Ambassador Holbrooke and Pickering on what ought to happen next, and Ambassador Pickering was very concerned about de-escalating the event at Racak and getting Serbian armoured vehicles and personnel and MUP out of the area, to calm it down, and back into their barracks. That's what I recall that statement meaning.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I was asking you about your contribution. "We must initiate Activation Order." That was my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that came translated as he's asking about this witness's contribution. There's nothing to indicate that this witness made a contribution. P has been identified as Pickering, not Phillips.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Have you got a further question, Mr. Djurdjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, but it's all in the notebook. There are perhaps one or two contributions by the witness; everything else was said by other people. It seems then we cannot ask him about it at all. I'm asking him about what it means, what it means to launch the Activation Order. In English it says "initiate ACTORD." I'm asking him whether -- or rather, what was his interpretation of Mr. Pickering's words. This is what he wrote down, the witness, and I'm asking him for an explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can I say, Mr. Djurdjic, that we have your explanation now of what you're asking, which is quite different from what the transcript says you're asking and that's happened several times and it's becoming most confusing. Colonel, the last four words on that page against the speaker P: "We must initiate ACTORD." Can you give us any understanding of the meaning of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. We knew when Racak occurred that our mission was in jeopardy. The Activation Order was a NATO Extraction Force that was in place to get us out safely. Ambassador Pickering was worried about obviously all the Americans has -- were the Permanent Council and their member states. It was agreed upon that NATO would be the Extraction Force for all of the member states, and when he refers to the Activation Order that's what that was about: Put them in Macedonia to receive us or to assist us in exiting Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Djurdjic, we have gone over an hour into this further session. It's been very slow progress and very little substance. Can you please concentrate your attention sharply on any further questions that you have for their relevance and importance.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, where were you on the 15th of January, 1999, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Were you perhaps in Montenegro visiting Mr. Djukanovic?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We visited him. I'd have to look at my notes to see exactly, but my point of being in Pristina, I was not in the United States is what I referenced that to. We were back in the theatre, in the mission area.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When was it that you heard of Racak for the first time?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it's in my notes, but I would have to tell you that it would have been on the 15th, shortly after it occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you know when the event took place?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We visited, I believe, the site on the 16th, at 7.00 in the morning, and I believe Racak occurred between the hours of 0700 and 1530 on the 15th.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that Mr. Walker came into his office on the 16th at 9.00 and that Mr. DZ said that around noon they set off for Racak?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there at Racak in the morning, and there was frost on the ground so it was early morning. Ambassador Walker was with me. We visited in the morning. It was very, very cold that day. You know, I can't speak to what Mr. DZ had said. My recollection is is we visited the site in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was DZ with you at that time?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure if he was or not. I don't recall, and if he was, he didn't go up into the ravine with us where the bodies were. But I don't recall if he went with us or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was General Maisonneuve with you?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe he was at Racak, yes, the morning of the 16th.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Were you notified that the police had informed the KVM that there was to be an operation in Racak?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember if we were notified or not, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know that two KVM vehicles were supposed to go to Racak village concerning that announcement?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any knowledge of that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When on the 16th of January you arrived in the village, were there any KLA in the village?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe we were met by the KLA. In fact, one of them identified himself as the commander and we met with him, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Does it mean that the village was under KLA control when you were there?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was our understanding that the village was a logistics depot for KLA for food and blankets and that sort of thing, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know that in and around the village there had -- there were 40 KLA members as of November 1998?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the numbers were. It was our understanding that the KLA did not use the village as a stronghold, but as a supply depot. They were -- they were out in the field and would come back. The women and children remained in the village, but they would come back to Racak for supplies.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What were the bunkers and trenches around Racak for?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably to protect the village I would imagine.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You spoke about some elderly people yesterday. You concluded they were civilians. Did you know that Sadik Mujota, aged 61, and Mehmet Mustafa, aged 62, were members of the KLA, having lost their lives in Racak on the 15th?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know those two individuals you mentioned personally no, or their ages. I don't know of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you know that in the village of Malo Poljica [as interpreted] that those killed in Racak were buried there as KLA members?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether they were or not. I don't have any information on what you're telling me on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Where did you get information to the effect that three females were killed -- that there were three woman in the 45 killed?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a KVM assessment from the team that had gone in there and counted the dead. There was also a 12-year-old boy that had been shot. I believe that those were the final reports from KVM.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, but why did you not wait for a few days for an investigation to determine what the facts were and then issue a press release? Instead, you issued a press release the very same day.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't issue the press release; Ambassador Walker did. And what he did I had no control over. We did ask for an immediate investigation and we did ask the Serbs for the names of those that participated in shelling the houses of the -- that contained women and children as well as young Serbian men and elder men. I think we requested an investigative team from Finland, and I believe we asked for Judge Arbour to come immediately, and of course that was met with many obstacles from the Serbian side.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know that only on the 18th of January there was an on-site investigation in Racak?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Investigation by whom? The Serb side or ... ?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: So three days after the event an investigation took place; is that what you're asking me?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you know that only after three days an investigating magistrate was able to go into Racak to carry out on on-site investigation?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew there was investigations taking place, but I also heard that they were incomplete and not satisfactory the way KVM understood investigations should proceed. I know Ambassador Walker wasn't happy with the manner that the investigations were taking place.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know that between the 15th in the afternoon and until the 18th KLA had control in Racak?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd have to be -- I'd have to read the reports. I'm not sure what the status of Racak was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. During the meeting with the commander, do you remember him saying to you that at 5.00 p.m. on the 15th Racak again fell under control of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't dispute it. Again, I'd have to refer to my notes, to trust my notes at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recall the commander acquainting you and Mr. Walker during that meeting that on the 15th of January he used mortars to attack Serb positions, Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember precisely, but I'll take your word for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. A journalist who was in Racak on the 16th with Mr. Walker and other KVM members was Mr. Franz Josef Hutsch. According to his words, when you arrived in Racak there were about a dozen KLA there. Do you recall them being there once you arrived?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do recall seeing some KLA. Some were wearing a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise. I forgot to go back into open session and we have been in closed session for a while now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Open.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can the notes be taken from the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that at the time when you visited Racak and its environs, the location was not secured for an on-site investigation?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Secured by -- by KVM or secured by the MUP? Secured at all? I'm ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: There was no MUP in Racak, that is -- that would mean that it would either have to be done by the verifiers or other members of the KVM who were in Racak. Did they secure the scene of crime in your knowledge when you were there?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I guess if you're asking me were there MUP around, no; was KVM there, yes. We had a number of verifiers that were taking reports of what events had occurred. Whether the site was secured or not as a crime scene, that wasn't in KVM's charter to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you notice the bodies of those killed being moved and that the spent shells, cartridges, were being taken away as souvenirs?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm aware of a couple of families that retrieved their loved ones from where they were killed and moved back into their -- into their homes for the bodies that were up in the ravine, they were -- we were told they were never touched or never moved, that was, they were shot and killed where they lay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know that on the 18th of January, 1999, there was an investigative magistrate of the district court in Pristina accompanied by Gil Gilbertson and a Mr. Sullivan who was an OSCE representative -- actually, both of them were?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Accompanied where exactly?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: To accompany the scene of crime team headed by the investigative judge of the district court in Pristina, her name is Danica Marinkovic.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do remember Ms. Marinkovic very, very well, and I am aware that the OSCE brought her to the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you know that the autopsies were also attended by OSCE representatives, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Djurdjic please repeat the two names of the OSCE representatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It seems I have to repeat the question. Colonel, did you know that the autopsies were also attended by OSCE representatives Ian Robert Hendrie from England and Mr. Pedersen from Denmark?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember if we attended those autopsies or not. There's no reason to dispute your claim there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know that members of the KLA kidnapped certain representatives of the Democratic League of Kosovo and they actually killed some of them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is this on the same day or at some other time?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I am leaving the topic of Racak, Colonel. This is an unrelated question to that topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can we have some indication of when, what year, what month?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, in the fall of 1998.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was aware that the KLA had committed acts of kidnapping and other violence. I'm not specifically aware of this particular event. They were certainly no saints.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You don't recall any activities by Mr. Walker and other members of the verification mission aimed at having those kidnapped by the KLA who were from Mr. Rugova's party released?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall the incident. I know we worked -- we worked a VJ release and we worked a KLA release, but I don't recall exactly who the kidnapped were. I know we had Serbian journalists and we had Serbian VJ that had been released. I don't recall the specifics of everyone that was kidnapped.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Colonel, sir, did you know that the KLA, after the signing of the October Agreements and the withdrawal of the VJ forces, took up positions which it had held before the summer operation?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the road between Pristina and Podujevo and then to Prokuplje used as the main vein to supply Kosovo and Metohija for both the civilians and the Army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware that the Prokuplje road was a key line of communication and line of transfer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that the end of your questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll finish the sentence. I'll tell you that after the break I wanted to ask Mr. Hannis if he could send me a bit more time and then after that conversation I'll be able to answer your question right after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, are you in a position to know how long your re-examination might be?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I think about 30 minutes, between 20 and 30 minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. If we break now, that's the time that is available for you, Mr. Djurdjic. I suggest we continue for another five minutes for you to finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Colonel, sir, the Yugoslav forces in the Podujevo area react to this by securing the area for further supplies and was this simply a reaction on -- to the KLA actions in that period and in that area?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were briefed that they were concerned about losing control of that particular strategic point to KLA control. And that briefing that we received was a verbal briefing in Podujevo from a VJ soldier I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know that the KLA, in addition to side-arms, also had anti-tank weapons?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you know that they also had guns that had a range of up to 3 to 4 kilometres?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was aware that they had weapons that went beyond 7.62 millimetres, yes. Precisely the kinds of weapons -- we're going through all this. I knew they had some mortar packs available to them, 7.62; I was aware of -- I never saw them but was aware that there was some anti-tank weapons available to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Since you were able to move around Kosovo, could you tell us, based on your experience, your military experience, what kind of fortifications did the Albanian houses in villages have? What types of walls and gates were there around them?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my experience, I didn't see anything out of the ordinary. I stayed in some of those homes. I'm not precisely sure what you're asking here. I mean, for me, it was a regular apartment and a regular home that had a -- typically had a gate to enter.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What about the compounds themselves, were they surrounded by high walls?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you refer to "compounds," what are you referring to? Are you referring to the normal living and housing areas in Pristina or are you talking about in the Drenica valley? What do you mean by "compounds"?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, what I said was the village homes, Albanian village homes; in other words, in villages, not in towns and cities. The walls that surrounded these houses, village houses, did you see how high they were and did you see them, the walls?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we visited KLA strongholds such as a facility we called the Ice House out of Drenica valley, what I observed in those areas was a fair number of KLA, armed. I don't recall the heights of the walls in general around any of their facility. That's not to say they weren't there, I just didn't -- I just don't remember them. I remember that it didn't seem -- wherever we went, it didn't seem like it was a fortified bunker or position of KLA soldiers. It just seemed like a normal living arrangement, a normal house, from what I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, on the topic of meetings with Milosevic, would you agree with me that you attended more of those meetings than Mr. Walker?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I attended one meeting without him. I believe that was in December. I attended one in November.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Would you take my word for it that Mr. Walker only mentions one meeting toward the end of October while you were -- when you were not there yet and another meeting with Mr. Milosevic on November 16th; and second, the chronology, the time-line that Mr. Drewienkiewicz drew up, there was only one meeting with Mr. Milosevic where Mr. Walker attended, jotted down, and that's the same meeting of November 16th. So there is no mention anywhere of any meeting in December, and I couldn't find any such mention in your notes either, and I read them through very carefully.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. I attended a meeting with Ambassador Holbrooke and Ambassador Miles that did not include Ambassador Walker. I thought that meeting was on December 15th. I attended a meeting with Ambassador Walker to see Mr. Milosevic in November, and I'm not sure if that was between the 23rd, 4th, or 5th, or on the 16th, but I was with Ambassador Walker on one of those visits.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Very well, Colonel. On the 15th of December you attended a meeting with Milosevic, that was the meeting with Mr. Holbrooke. That was on December 15th, 1998. And let me just say one more thing and this is even in your notes. The letter of Mr. Walker's of November 23rd was not actually taken and submitted at this meeting, but it was sent only later on, on the 25th. And let me also remind you that you had a couple of meetings with Mr. Sainovic where you discussed this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry, objection. That doesn't sound like a question; that sounds like testimony from Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Same old problem, Mr. Djurdjic. If you want the witness to agree that the letter was not handed over at the meeting, you need to put that to him and he'll say yes or no. You can't put it to him as a fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. What I'm trying to do is just refresh his memory regarding some of these circumstances, but I can also ask him whether I'm correct or not. I think in the final analysis it comes down to the same thing. So I was just trying to jog his memory because the witness said that this letter was actually handed in to Milosevic at this meeting on the 23rd, but in fact it was on the 24th or the 25th. And I even have your notes here, but I can't find the exact spot to show that this letter was actually handed in on the 25th well, never mind. Just tell us, Witness, do you remember this or not?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember the letter. My memory serves me that it very well may have been that we gave that letter up through embassy channels and it went through officially and Ambassador Walker carried his own copy of the letter. My recollection is is that he gave him that letter and discussed that letter. It's possible that I could be wrong, but I know that we talked about that letter in there and I remember Ambassador Walker saying it was going to be the purpose of his visit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel, for answering my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours for allowing me additional time for my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djurdjic. We need to have a break now with those tapes, Mr. Hannis, but what we will do is resume at ten minutes past and hope you'll be able to finish in the 20 minutes, which was the lower end of your estimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'll do my very best, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hannis. We resume at ten minutes past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will be very brief, Your Honours, and this has to do with the exhibits, or rather, the documents that we propose to be admitted into evidence, D004-4172 and D004-4175, they should be admitted into evidence without a stamp, and all the other documents that were on the list should be admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, if that's the agreement of counsel they will be admitted and exhibit numbers will be assigned and you'll be informed by memo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please sit. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. My first questions are regarding the notebook, so if we could go into private.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Colonel, I'd like to look at your notebook which is P1312 and I'd first like to look at page 30 of the English. It's page 36 in the B/C/S. Colonel, this will be up on the screen in a minute, but it's referring to your notes dated the 9th of January. And I want to ask about some points under the heading at 0734 hours. Now, I note that this January 9th is one day after we saw that press release this Exhibit D162 about some MUP that were killed and injured between Suva Reka and Stimlje. Do you remember Mr. Djurdjic showing you that one?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the second entry here says: "KVM going back to negotiate the release of at least two VJ soldiers." You told us earlier in your testimony about this group of eight or nine VJ soldiers that had wandered off and been captured. Is that -- do you know when they were released approximately?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were released before the 15th of January.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And the next entry says: "I read the 8 Jan 99 press statement calling the KLA terrorists for the taking of eight VJ as POWs." That's a different press release than the one we saw in D162, which was about the killing of MUP. And I don't think you saw that press statement while we were in here in the past couple of days, did you? I haven't seen it?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't seen it, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The next entry says: "Unfortunate statement from KVM and it could play right into the hands of Belgrade." Is that referring to the press statement calling the KLA terrorists for capture of the eight VJ? Or for the killing of MUP or --

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That refers to the KLA terrorists, and again the key word there was "terrorists."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was what was unfortunate. We didn't want that in our press releases because we had made a judgement what they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And the next entry says: "Call Wes Clark and pass to NATO - mention this is an unfortunate press statement and made by our French deputy." I think you told us that was Ambassador Keller?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Keller, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did he make one statement or two statements where he referred to KLA as terrorists, if you --

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ambassador Keller?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He always referred to the KLA as terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whenever it was --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers kindly pause between questions and answers for the interpreters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To follow-up, Ambassador Keller always referred to the KLA as terrorists. He was cautioned by Ambassador Walker that whether it be in written statements, press statements, or verbal statements, that was not our position to take, and he and Ambassador Keller had words on that issue several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The next line says: "This is a bad precedent for future negotiations." Was that refer -- did that have any reference to negotiations about releasing the VJ hostages or was it in a broader -- broader context?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to tell you, sir, that that would be in a broader context. If KVM was calling the KLA "terrorists," it wasn't likely we were going to get any progress or negotiation progress with them. So it was in a broader context.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But were negotiations about the VJ eight or nine going on at this time?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'd like to go to the next page in English, page 31, and that's page 38 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You'll see this is from a meeting on the 10th of January at 0740. I had a question about this because it's unclear to me about when you were on leave in the US and when you were back. This says a meeting with Sainovic. Do you recall, were you back in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I took these notes, I was definitely back. So I'm not sure of the hour that we arrived, but I would have been back by the 10th, having taken these notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And the notes from the day before, on the 9th, were those notes you made pursuant to phone calls that were going back and forth from where you were in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could have been, yes, it could have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. At the bottom of the page in English on this one --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I think we have to go to page 39 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: -- this entry about "Walker talked with Wes Clark." It says: "Very worried the press is playing this as the KLA is to blame because it undercuts his NATO authority." Who were you referred to as being worried there? Was it Walker or Clark or somebody else?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This would have been Wes Clark being worried.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I say it says "his authority." I assume Walker had no authority in NATO or over NATO?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Next if we could go to page 34 in the English, that's page 41 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: This is 16 January at 1634 hours. This is right after Racak. I see the second line says: "This event and the Decani incident are not related." Now, I think that relates to the press release we saw in Exhibit D161, which was also something that took place, I think, on the 15th of January, where KVM personnel were shot at?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And do you know what the information was to show that that was not related to Racak?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't -- I don't recall what caused me to link the -- you know, the two events. I believe it was the RC commander, isolated event.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I can see why that connection might be drawn that -- didn't you tell us before that some components of the KLA thought that KVM was responsible in part for what happened at Racak? Or am I misremembering?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm trying to remember. I remember the discussion. I remember being, you know, being blamed by the KLA for in part what happened. I'm having trouble trying to remember why, but I do remember that discussion, that we were being blamed for what had happened and that we weren't there in large numbers and we weren't protecting that village, we didn't have a presence; and had we been there, that might not have happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I think you said Racak was sort of the low point in the mission's history up to that point?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And it was particularly painful because it was on the heels of your high point in getting those VJ --

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- released.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: -- soldiers released?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Which is the next entry about: "Three to four days ago KLA released eight ... and this is the result." If you could go down to the first entry for letter H which I think you told us stands for Holbrooke --

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: -- in this context. It says: "Press for immediate release of KLA POWs." Do you know what that refers to?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The VJ had captured eight KLA, and we were trying to win their release unharmed. We struck a deal with Serb authorities, but the Serb authorities did not want the release appear to be connected to the VJ release, although it was, but it was a quid pro quo, but the Serbs wanted to maintain an image of strength and wanted the two completely separated to appear that they weren't linked.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I understand. So this was the delayed release to avoid the appearance that Serbia was negotiating with what they deemed terrorists?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And now, in light of what had happened in Racak, Holbrooke is suggesting: Release -- make Serbia release them now?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: To, what, calm down KLA --

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just to get the situation under control and get people to calm down.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could go to the next page, 35 in English and page 42 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It's still the same meeting and Holbrooke is the speaker. The first entry: "Need to do a formal report to NATO/OSCE on non-compliance." Mr. Djurdjic asked you some questions about a provision in the agreement about reporting. Do you recall, was there a formal report that was written and sent to OSCE after this?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was. It went to the Permanent Council. I think that Ambassador Walker even flew down there to brief it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And while we're still in private session, I wanted to follow-up on those reportings. You were asked yesterday by Mr. Djurdjic about reporting, and in one of your answers where you were talking about letters of protest about non-compliance you said at page 84, line 16: "I remember some documents that Mr. Walker wanted on the record that clearly defined non-compliance issues. One was in the form of a letter that went in December, verbally, primarily to Mr. Milosevic." When you say "verbally, primarily," how does that work with a letter? Do you understand? I see letter as something written. Do you hand it to him and tell him what's in it or ...?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ambassador Walker would often make his notes and what he wanted to say. If -- you know, about the letter that's in question here -- he certainly may have given a letter of non-compliance to make Ambassador Miles in the embassy and of course State Department aware of it through that channel, as he would the Permanent Council but also delivered verbally his unhappiness with the non-compliance issues that we were struggling with to Mr. Milosevic. So I would tell you that it would be both written and it would be verbal.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. And near the end of your testimony you were asked about the letters being delivered to Mr. Milosevic, and it was suggested to you that one was delivered to him in December, I think on the 15th, when you and Miles and Holbrooke met with Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I think you testified that you recalled that Walker had also delivered that 23 November letter about definitions and sort of broad parameters of the KVM mission sometime in late November, when you and he met with Milosevic; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I see Mr. Djurdjic on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll be brief. I was referring to the letter of November 23rd, and I never mentioned any letter of December.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Neither am I.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: My question is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on, please, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: My question is: Is it possible that the letter of the 23rd of November was delivered on both dates, first by Mr. Walker in late November and later on by Holbrooke and Miles?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible. When Mr. Holbrooke came into town he took a lot of information with him, the DMZ, Malisevo map, some KVM reporting, I wasn't in the room when he delivered a lot of that material, but it definitely would be possible. That would be typical of Mr. Holbrooke.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And by doing so, that's a more formal presentation than it coming from Mr. Walker?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which is why Mr. Walker wasn't present.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And based on your experience in dealing with the federal commission for cooperation with the OSCE, did sometimes Sainovic and the others insist on strict technicalities and formalities when you were running into obstacles about getting them things resolved?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Constant technicality issues, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We can go back into open now, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Open.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Just a few more, Colonel. You were asked about what the KVM did in relation to stop weapons smuggling. Did KVM have any authority to deal with weapons being smuggled into Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Who was that a job for in Serbia, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would think that the border guards would be in large part responsible for those weapons that were coming in.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Next you were shown yesterday at page 92, line 10, Exhibit D160, which is UN Resolution 1199. I won't pull it up. I'll read. You were shown paragraph 4(a) and Mr. Djurdjic asked you if you would agree that that only called on Yugoslavia to cease all action. And his question was: "Q. Only in relation to the civilian population and to withdraw security units." I would indicate to you that the document -- the UN Resolution says: "Cease all action by the security forces affecting the civilian population." My question is: Those joint VJ and MUP actions that you saw in Kosovo, even though they may have been directed at KLA, in the manner in which they were carried out were those actions affecting the civilian population?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: They absolutely were. They were, in general, sweep operations. And by "sweep" I mean they included all personnel, all people, population, in the village. It didn't discriminate between the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. And the last one I want to ask you about, Exhibit 835, which is the agreement about the KVM mission. Mr. Djurdjic made the point that the primary purpose was to maintain the cease-fire?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I have a question. In your efforts to verify whether there was compliance with the cease-fire, did KVM requests from Mr. Sainovic and that group that you met with that you be advised in advance when there were going to be movements of MUP or VJ in carrying out some of these anti-terrorist actions?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we had asked for advanced notice. At least 24 hours we had asked for.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And did Mr. Sainovic agree to do that?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Was that important to you in being able to carry out your job?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very much important to us, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Because if you were only going to be notified a week after that occurred, how would that help you do any verification?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was one of the frustrations of the mission. We just didn't get timely coordination for being able to be in front of some of these operations or accompany these operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And if you only got reports a week after they happened, you might as well have been in Hawaii as Pristina?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that, Mr. Hannis. You'll be pleased to know that that's the end of the run.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We would like to thank you for coming once again, for the assistance you have been able to give. You are free to return to your normal activities. The Court Officer will show you out. We would thank those who have assisted you in your time here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We are at the point of an adjournment for some two weeks. We hope in that time, A, Mr. Hannis, the Prosecution will be able not only to review its case and its position to be sure and have clearly in its mind what else needs to be done so that there is no further hiccup in the presentation of the Prosecution case.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'll convey that to the team, Your Honour, and we'll make our best efforts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good. And efforts are made to ensure the witnesses are here. In the last couple of weeks we've been slipping fairly badly on performance and losing time. We would hope that can be behind us now and things will move along. While this break will be of immediate assistance to the Prosecution, it's also one that should assist the Defence a great deal in collecting your thoughts and finalising your preparation with a view to the steps that need to be taken when the Prosecution case finishes, and if necessary to -- looking ahead to the preparation and presentation of the Defence case. As we have indicated that should that be the course taken, it will -- should not be expected that there'll be a long break between the end of the Prosecution case and the start of the Defence case. We want to keep the trial moving, so we would encourage Defence counsel to be giving thought ahead during this fortnight's break. With those words of encouragement, we hope that the break is of assistance to all parties and we resume again on Tuesday afternoon, the 22nd, I think, Courtroom I, I'm told. So we look forward to seeing you then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 22nd day of September, 2009, at 2.15 p.m.
